newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Laos wants Indonesian aircraft, Murdiono says.
newsitem.headline: Laos wants Indonesian aircraft, Murdiono says.

text.p: Lao Prime Minister Khamtay Siphandone said his country wanted to buy planes and helicopters from Indonesia but there was a question mark over the method of payment, Indonesian State Secretary Murdiono said on Thursday.

"Laos has said it wanted to buy aircraft and helicopters from Indonesia. This needs careful study, especially on the methods of payment," Murdiono told reporters after a meeting between Khamtay and President Suharto.
"Indonesia has offered a counter-trade proposal if Laos is unable to pay in cash," he added.
"Indonesia is importing around 600,000 tonnes of soybeans annually. If Laos can develop soybean production, certainly we will have the opportunity to buy from Laos," Murdiono said.

Indonesia currently builds the CN-235 twin-engined commuter aircraft. The state-owned aircraft company Industri Pesawat Terbang Nusantara (IPTN) also makes French-designed Puma and U.S. Bell helicopters under licence.
Khamtay arrived on Wednesday and will attend an informal summit of leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nation (ASEAN) on Saturday.
ASEAN groups Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore, Philippines and Brunei. Laos, Cambodia and Burma currently have observer status.
